claims.explanation: Desoxycortone is a mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) agonist, and its selective killing pattern tracks with intact mineralocorticoid receptor signaling and epithelial/steroid-responsive lineage context rather than any single driver mutation. The most sensitive lines are predominantly TP53-mutant epithelial carcinomas (skin, lung, gastric, colorectal, esophageal, endometrial, ovarian), while resistant lines include mesenchymal/neuroendocrine tumors and several lines with PI3K-pathway or NRAS activation that may bypass MR-dependent growth suppression. The virtual-cell signature (up STAT3/NFATC3, down cell-cycle genes CCNB2/CDC20) is consistent with MR-mediated transcriptional reprogramming and cell-cycle arrest in responsive epithelial lines.

features.basis: Drug is an NR3C2 agonist; receptor expression is required for response
Nearly all most-killed lines carry TP53 mutation; loss of p53 may remove a brake on steroid-induced growth arrest/apoptosis
Annotated target; glucocorticoid receptor cross-talk can mediate mineralocorticoid ligand effects
PI3K-pathway activation appears enriched in least-affected lines (HGC27, MKN1, SNU840)
PTEN loss/PI3K activation in several resistant lines (786O, UACC62, HEC265, FTC133)
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) are among least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven bypass
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/gastric lines (SNU410, T3M4, GSU) are resistant
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (LOXIMVI, UACC62, K029AX) are least affected
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) appear in the sensitive set
Recurrent in several most-killed squamous/gastric lines, possibly reflecting chromatin state permissive to steroid response
Co-occurring with TP53 in several sensitive lines; cell-cycle deregulation may enhance arrest
Virtual-cell signature shows STAT3 upregulation, consistent with MR-mediated transcriptional response
